alt: Mirror-gloss epoxy floor in a showroom of classic cars

problems: The floor in A looks like a pasted-on texture. The cracks, oil stains and green-brown patches look painted on and repeat unnaturally.
The stains and cracks look too stylized and dramatic, and they cover the floor more evenly than real wear would.
The floor in A has no reflections of the cars, lights or walls. The cars look pasted onto the floor, and the contact shadows under them are weak or inconsistent.
The car tires and bumpers on the near left and right edges blend into the floor texture without a realistic grounding shadow.
The floor looks too uniformly dirty and too 'HDR'. It does not match the soft ambient lighting of the rest of the scene, which is unchanged between the two images.
Some small debris items (yellow and white bits) near the right side look artificial.
The floor damage looks exaggerated and unrealistic: oil-like brown and orange stains, a web of cracks, and a wet, glossy sheen. It looks like a texture overlay, not real concrete.
The cars don't sit on the damaged floor convincingly. There are no contact shadows or tire marks, and the floor doesn't reflect the cars, so they look pasted on.
The floor texture doesn't follow the perspective. The cracks and stains look flat and don't shrink toward the back of the room.
A real showroom floor with this much damage would be very unlikely, because the cars are parked in neat rows. A homeowner would see it as staged or fake.
The stains look plastic and blotchy, with a repeating pattern in the oil patches.
